analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3) and adds one row at head line 372, 'Active-store victim selection', documenting the eviction algorithm (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot). The row says eviction picks the oldest entry by a linear probe with lexicographic tag tie-break. If the first retirement fails, it falls back to one snapshot taken after the first attempt and iterates a binary heap in the same order. External-removal reconciliation stops the pass so the budget can recheck usage. I found no changes to code, keys, TTL (still 1800s per the TTL row, within the T-041/SEC-035 sign-off), disk-budget rules, DBK3 format, HMAC naming or epoch handling. The description is consistent with T-041 mitigations: eviction remains LRU by last hit over the kv3 root, per-file removals do not rotate the epoch, and the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge. It adds no new attack surface, and the wording makes no new security claim that contradicts the threat model. Limits: the referenced Swift sources are not supplied, so I could not verify that the documented algorithm matches the code. I also could not check for local DoS from O(n) snapshot copies under large indexes. That is a performance matter and not a security regression. The base units (3 and 4) are unchanged context that carries the other rows, and the head unit 5 is the only portion with edits. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the range map is complete with only lines 3 and 372 changed.
